value.text: {"result": {"suggestions": [{"kind": "new_thesis", "ticker": "GOOGL", "statement": "YouTube advertising, led by connected-TV demand, takes budget share from linear TV and other platforms and grows on its own track, apart from Search.", "wrong_if": "Reported YouTube commitments and CTV pricing slow, or agencies report that incremental budget is not shifting from linear TV and Meta.", "driver_ids": ["GOOGL.services_growth"], "rationale": "An agency channel check reports faster YouTube commitments and budget shifting from linear TV and Meta, while the existing pillars cover only Search click loss, capex margin pressure and regulatory remedies, none of which address YouTube or CTV share gains.", "claim_ids": ["synthetic_000177.c1", "synthetic_000177.c4"], "sections": [{"email_id": "synthetic_000177", "quote": "Q4 YouTube commitments across his book are up roughly 24% y/y, against ~14% growth in Q3."}, {"email_id": "synthetic_000177", "quote": "About one-third of the incremental budget is coming from linear TV and Meta, which he calls a \"measurable\" shift, aided by the new cross-device attribution reporting."}]}], "no_change_reason": null}}
